questions.question: How does Pakistan's National Cyber Security Policy 2021 treat cyber-attacks on critical infrastructure and respond to them?

criteria.description: Treats CI/CII cyber-attacks as aggression against national sovereignty
criteria.source_excerpt: Will regard a cyber-attack on Pakistan CI/ CII as an act of aggression against national sovereignty

criteria.description: Defends itself with appropriate response measures
criteria.source_excerpt: will defend itself with appropriate response measures.

questions.rationale: Tests a specific national-policy statement, not an invented list of defensive actions.

questions.question: What is the vision of Pakistan's National Cyber Security Policy 2021?

criteria.description: Secure, robust, continually improving nationwide digital ecosystem
criteria.source_excerpt: The vision is for Pakistan to have a secure, robust, and continually improving nationwide digital ecosystem

criteria.description: Confidentiality, integrity, and availability of digital assets
criteria.source_excerpt: ensuring accountable confidentiality, integrity, and availability of digital assets

criteria.description: Socio-economic development and national security
criteria.source_excerpt: leading to socio-economic development and national security.

questions.rationale: Tests vision coverage rather than treating a related governance passage as a complete answer.

questions.question: What oversight and policy-formulation functions does Pakistan's Cyber Governance Policy Committee (CGPC) have?

criteria.description: Strategic oversight over national cybersecurity issues
criteria.source_excerpt: Cyber Governance Policy Committee is responsible for strategic oversight over national Cyber Security issues.

criteria.description: Formulate, guide, and recommend approval of policy and Act
criteria.source_excerpt: Formulate, guide, and recommend for the approval of the National Cyber Security Policy and Cyber Security Act.

criteria.description: Guide updates and periodic reviews for emerging cyberspace requirements
criteria.source_excerpt: Guide to align policy with emerging cyberspace requirements through updates and periodic reviews.

questions.rationale: Tests coverage of separate governance functions in a single verified source page.

questions.question: How does NIST CSF 2.0 address incident response plan execution, incident triage, and prioritization?

criteria.description: Execute the plan with relevant third parties after declaration
criteria.source_excerpt: The incident response plan is executed in coordination with relevant third parties once an incident is declared

criteria.description: Triage and validate reports
criteria.source_excerpt: Incident reports are triaged and validated

criteria.description: Categorize and prioritize incidents
criteria.source_excerpt: Incidents are categorized and prioritized

questions.rationale: Tests three explicit RS.MA outcomes; matching the RESPOND heading alone is incomplete.

questions.question: What does NIST CSF 2.0 say about verifying backup and restored-system integrity during recovery?

criteria.description: Verify backups/restoration assets before use
criteria.source_excerpt: The integrity of backups and other restoration assets is verified before using them for restoration

criteria.description: Verify restored assets and confirm normal operations
criteria.source_excerpt: The integrity of restored assets is verified, systems and services are restored, and normal operating status is confirmed

questions.rationale: Tests recovery controls, including the distinction between checking backups and restored systems.

questions.question: Under NIST CSF 2.0 DE.AE-08, when are incidents declared?

criteria.description: Declare incidents when adverse events meet defined incident criteria
criteria.source_excerpt: Incidents are declared when adverse events meet the defined incident criteria

questions.rationale: Tests a precise DETECT outcome; no real incident or numerical score should be invented.

questions.question: In the CyberSage synthetic casebook CS-INC-002, how was ransomware detected, contained, and recovered from, and was a ransom paid?

criteria.description: Rapid renaming and unsigned encryption process
criteria.source_excerpt: Endpoint telemetry detected rapid file renaming and an unsigned encryption process on a shared drive.

criteria.description: Workstation isolated and compromised credentials disabled
criteria.source_excerpt: Isolated the workstation, disabled compromised credentials, restored affected files from a verified offline backup.

criteria.description: Restore affected files from verified offline backup
criteria.source_excerpt: restored affected files from a verified offline backup.

criteria.description: Recovery completed without ransom payment
criteria.source_excerpt: Files on one departmental share were encrypted; recovery completed without ransom payment.

questions.rationale: Tests multi-chunk incident coverage and explicit synthetic/fictional labeling; triage labels are not evidence of outcome.

questions.question: In the CyberSage synthetic casebook CS-INC-017, what happened to the five backup deletion requests and what containment controls were applied?

criteria.description: All five requests failed and restore points remained available
criteria.source_excerpt: All five deletion requests failed; restore points remained available.

criteria.description: Disable service token
criteria.source_excerpt: Disabled the service token, enforced immutable backups, and restricted delete permissions to a break-glass role.

criteria.description: Immutable backups and restricted break-glass deletion permissions
criteria.source_excerpt: enforced immutable backups, and restricted delete permissions to a break-glass role.

questions.rationale: Tests confirmed outcome versus a mere attempted deletion, with synthetic incident labeling.

questions.question: What is the cybersecurity policy of Mars in 2050?
questions.rationale: No indexed PDF documents a Martian cybersecurity policy. Require explicit insufficient evidence with no citations.

questions.question: What is the exact SHA-256 hash of the malware used in CyberSage casebook incident CS-INC-002?
questions.rationale: The case record describes ransomware but supplies no malware SHA-256. Require abstention rather than an invented hash.
